title: Release train decision matrix and deterministic scope-lock cadence for API / Console / Runtime
creator: Priya Sethi
description:
Purpose: Establish a deterministic cadence and decision matrix for the upcoming integrated release of API, Console, and Runtime to reduce ad-hoc scope changes, accelerate go/no-go calls, and make release notes coordination reproducible across GTM, Docs, and Support.

Scope: Milestone definitions, formal scope-lock gates, a cutline decision matrix (quantitative + qualitative signals), responsibilities for release notes and collateral, a lightweight rollback/runbook template, and a small experiment to pilot a two-week visible freeze window for user-facing UX changes.

Goals:
- Make scope-lock calls predictable and auditable (timestamp + decision rationale).
- Reduce last-minute feature churn by 60% versus previous release measured by PRs merged inside freeze window.
- Shorten release notes compilation time from 5 days to 2 days via templated ownership and pre-approved bullets.

Non-goals: Deep technical runtime refactor work (large ABI changes) and onboarding of new major models — those will follow separate channel releases.
acceptance_criteria: Decision matrix documented in Confluence with owner signatures (PM/Eng/Design) and timestamped sign-off
Cutline automation set up: release checklist shows PASS/FAIL per signal (telemetry, e2e, perf) for the final cut call
Release notes draft with owner-assigned bullets for every visible change present 72 hours before planned ship
Rollback runbook created and validated with a smoke test (internal canary) and a <30m known rollback path
release_signals: Telemetry: error-rate (5xx) baseline change <= 2x and absolute 5xx rate below 0.5% across sampled routes
Latency: p95 for gen endpoint within 1.25x of baseline and p95 under 1200ms for hosted tier
Throughput: Dedicated capacity autoscaler exercised in preflight load test with no queue growth > 10% over 30m
E2E: Console flows (login, model selection, rollout toggle) pass smoke with no flaky tests > 2 failures in last 24h
Regression: QA regression harness shows <=1 critical test failing and all failures triaged
Docs/Notes: Release notes draft present and reviewed by Docs, PM, and Support
cut_criteria_matrix: Green: All release_signals PASS => Full cut (ship planned feature set)
Yellow: 1 non-blocking signal degraded (telemetry margin exceeded OR 1 flaky e2e) => Mitigation plan required + timeboxed hold (max 48h). PM + ENG lead decision required.
Red: Any blocking signal (persistent error spike >2x baseline, p95 double baseline, or failing critical e2e) => Delay release; implement fallback or revert candidate PRs. Rollback runbook staged.
Scope change rule: Any new user-visible feature proposed inside freeze window requires a P0 bug or legal/regulatory justification and written approval from PM, ENG owner, and Security if applicable.
Docs rule: If docs/release notes gaps exceed 25% of visible changes, release is paused until coverage >= 75% or a temporary public note vendor is arranged.
Emergency patches: Security-critical fixes may bypass feature freeze but must follow a dedicated emergency release lane with cross-functional notification and postmortem within 3 business days.
coordination_notes: Owners: PM (Priya Sethi) coordinates the cut call; ENG lead (Ethan Park) owns telemetry/perf signals; Design (Maya Lin) owns UX verification; Docs (Alex Martin) compiles release notes; Support (Daniel O'Reilly) prepares customer-facing comms.

Timeline:
- T-21d: Feature list locked by engineering (shippable scope), drafts for release notes started.
- T-10d: Preflight perf and load run; initial QA regression completed.
- T-5d: Docs release notes first full draft; GTM comms review.
- T-2d: Final cut call window opens; decision matrix evaluated and timestamped.
- Ship day: Release window + post-deploy monitoring + 4h watch rotation.
- +3d: Post-release telemetry review and incident triage (if any).

Artifacts: Confluence plan: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RT/PM-20987; Release notes draft: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB-example; Preflight load PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1247
Release notes template: Use the standardized bullets: What changed, Why it matters, Migration notes (if any), Known issues, Contact/support link. Owners should fill their bullets before T-5d.
GTM: Marketing to publish blog + product changelog within 24h of ship. Customer success to notify top 25 customers with potential impact ahead of release (T-2d).
risk_register: Risk: Late performance regression discovered in specialized enterprise workloads. Mitigation: Maintain a preflight replica of dedicated pools; if regression > cutoff, route enterprise customers to previous model variant via smart routing for 72h.
Risk: Missing release notes for critical UX changes. Mitigation: Mandatory bullet ownership assigned at T-21d; escalate missing bullets at T-5d to PMG lead.
Risk: Autoscaler misconfiguration during ramp. Mitigation: Run controlled autoscale stress tests at T-10d and keep burst capacity reserved for first 24h.
Risk: Post-release bug that requires rollback. Mitigation: Short rollback path validated; tagging and revert PR process rehearsed in a dry-run during this cycle.
